sections.html:
Anniston is the county seat of Calhoun County and Oxford is its biggest city; together they make up the Anniston-Oxford metro area in east central Alabama. The 2020 census counted 116,441 residents, and the 2025 estimate of 115,834 shows almost no change. With a steady population, the people who buy your house will mostly be locals.

The 2020 housing count shows 46,437 households sharing 53,052 units, with 12.5 percent of units empty. Homeowners fill 68.4 percent of the occupied homes. Rental vacancy runs 12.2 percent, so a rental house can stay empty for months. An inherited or tenant-worn rental feels that pinch before an owner-occupied family home does. Rural living is common too, since 36.5 percent of residents are outside urban areas.

Watch the county lines. Glencoe and Southside lie partly in Etowah County, Oxford reaches into Talladega and Cleburne counties, and Piedmont reaches into Cherokee County. An Oxford or Glencoe mailing address can therefore belong to a different county's tax rolls than you would guess, and the parcel record settles it. School districts are split by city instead of by county: Anniston City, Calhoun County, Jacksonville City, Oxford City and Piedmont City.

Bills come due October 1, and any balance left after December 31 is delinquent. The state calendar then runs on its own: the probate court receives the account in February, meets in March, advertises in April and holds the tax sale in May.

The Revenue Commissioner mails statements as a favor, not an obligation, and a lost bill cancels nothing. Houses that sat vacant through an estate or after a tenant moved out are the ones most likely to slide into this calendar unnoticed.

Changes to the property can shift the assessment. Built a deck or a garage? Expect the value to move, and tell the commissioner's office about additions when it asks.

Your first move is a written protest sent to the county Board of Equalization, due 30 days after your valuation notice arrives. Code of Alabama sections 40-3-20, 40-3-24 and 40-3-25 govern the process.

StepDeadline
Written protest to the Board of Equalization30 days after the valuation notice
Appeal to circuit court30 days after the board's final ruling
Jury demand10 days after the appeal is taken

Going to court under section 40-3-25 means giving notice to the board secretary and the circuit court clerk and posting a bond the clerk approves. Pay the taxes due, figured on last year's assessment, before they turn delinquent. If you skip that, the court may dismiss your appeal unless you put up a supersedeas bond. Filing an appeal never halts collection, so anyone who appeals and sells in the same year should plan to cover the bill from the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: Online services and the commission office
sections.html:
The county website takes property tax payments online by check or credit card. It also hosts a GIS map with appraisal details searchable by owner or address, and a portal for business personal property. Boat and manufactured home decals and business licenses can be renewed there. Manufactured home renewals run in October and November.

Use the GIS map to look up your own parcel before you talk to a buyer, since it shows what the county has on record. Paying online is handy if closing is near and one bill is still open.

The commission meets in the Ken Joiner Administration Building at 1702 Noble Street in Anniston. The Revenue Commissioner has a tab of its own on the county site, which is the right place to begin with assessing questions.

sections.h2: Recording tax when a house sells
sections.html:
Section 40-22-1 sets the deed tax at 50 cents for every $500 of value conveyed, and a leftover fraction counts as a whole unit. The probate office, which accepts the deed and collects the tax, adds a separate recording fee.

Value already covered by a mortgage on which the mortgage tax was paid is left out, so the final tax can come in under the simple math. Each deed must also carry proof of the actual price, using a Department of Revenue form that the signer attests to. Have your title company calculate the number ahead of closing so it appears on the settlement statement.

Three situations cause most of the grief: a house needing repairs, an estate with several heirs and a rental left empty. Conventional listings lean on an appraisal, a lender and a patient buyer, and each situation strains at least one of them.

A sensible order of work looks like this.

  1. Look up the parcel and note which county sends the bill.
  2. Find out if the current year is paid and if any earlier year is still open.
  3. Round up the deed, the newest tax statement and probate papers when heirs are involved.
  4. Have the title company quote a payoff for each open year.

Selling for cash removes the lender and the appraisal from the picture. We purchase Calhoun County houses in any condition and can talk through unpaid tax on our first call. Whatever is owed is typically settled from your proceeds at the closing table, so there is nothing to scrape together beforehand.

Heirs need special attention. Where several people share a house, each usually has to sign, and the title company asks for proof of who inherited. Begin that paperwork at once, because tracking down a distant relative or a missing record is what drags a sale out. If the tax is already delinquent, tell every heir at the outset.

sections.h2: What to ask the county before you sell
sections.html:
A short phone call can save a closing. Reach the Revenue Commissioner's office and ask four plain questions. Which tax years show as owed on this parcel? Has any addition or removal been reported that could change the value? Is a protest pending? What name and mailing address does the county hold for the owner? A mismatch in that last answer is common after a death or a divorce, and it explains why bills sometimes go astray.

Keep the replies in one folder together with your deed. If the house is a rental, add the lease status and a note on whether anyone is living there. A buyer who sees a clear paper trail can move faster, and so can you. Anniston is where you will go in person, so allow time for parking and a wait at the counter, and bring photo identification in case staff need to confirm who you are.

faqs.q: What are the Calhoun County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. The tax sale follows in May after the probate court steps in February, March and April.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Calhoun County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the written valuation notice to protest to the Board of Equalization. After a final board decision, a circuit court appeal must be taken within another 30 days.

faqs.q: Do I owe property tax if I never got a bill in Calhoun County?
faqs.a: Yes. Revenue Commissioners mail notices only as a courtesy, and the tax is owed whether or not a statement arrives.

faqs.q: Why might my Oxford or Glencoe house be taxed by another county?
faqs.a: Several Calhoun County cities cross a county line. Oxford is partly in Talladega and Cleburne counties and Glencoe is partly in Etowah County, so check the parcel record.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Calhoun County house that still has taxes due?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. Open taxes are normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Call us with the parcel number and we will look at what is owed before talking about an offer.
